issues.description: The problem statement's UML and task text indicate getTotalNumberOfStudents() should return an int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning a StudentCount object (and adds a StudentCount class). This introduces a structural mismatch: students guided by the UML/template will expect an int return type while the solution uses a custom wrapper type, which can confuse implementations and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent with the UML/problem statement. Either (A) change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (remove or stop using the StudentCount wrapper) and update dependent methods accordingly, or (B) update the problem statement and template to document and provide the StudentCount type (including its API) so the use of a wrapper is intentional. Prefer option (A) to match the current UML and keep the template minimal.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and task text) specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents() returns an int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object (and adds a StudentCount class). This represents the same conceptual entity (the total number of students) with two different identifiers/types (primitive int vs StudentCount), which can confuse students about the expected return type and how to implement the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation of the "total number of students" consistent across artifacts. Either (a) change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (and remove the StudentCount wrapper), or (b) update the problem statement and UML to specify a StudentCount return type and explicitly introduce the StudentCount concept. Prefer aligning with the UML and text (return int) unless the StudentCount wrapper is intentionally part of the exercise and then update the documentation accordingly.
